body:
# EngineShelf 1.1.9

## Fixed

- **"This script contains malicious content and has been blocked by your
  antivirus software."** 1.1.8 would not start at all on a Windows machine whose
  Defender objected to `gui\server.ps1`. Windows scans a PowerShell file through
  AMSI before it compiles it, so nothing of ours had run: the whole manager came
  back as a parse error pointing at line 1 of a file whose line 1 is
  `[CmdletBinding()]`, with "Press any key to continue" under it. Windows only -
  there is no AMSI on the other half, and `gui/server.py` was never affected.

  It is a false positive, and one this manager can genuinely collect: it listens
  on a loopback port and starts hidden PowerShell children, which is most of what
  a backdoor does. It could not be reproduced on the machine this was fixed on,
  so rather than aim at a signature nobody has measured, the two things worth
  removing were removed. The manager had three copies of the same child command
  line - the catalog refresh, the availability refresh, and every job - and has
  one now, in `Start-Child`, which asks for no window at all instead of asking
  for one and hiding it. `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` stays: the child is a new
  `powershell.exe`, the default policy on Windows client is Restricted, and
  without it no job would run on any machine nobody had told otherwise.

- **The catalog and availability refreshes could hang with nothing in the log.**
  Both started a child that inherited the manager's stdin, so anything that
  stopped to ask a question waited for an answer that could not arrive, and
  neither child had anywhere to write what it printed. Every job already got an
  empty stdin and a log of its own; these two, which are not jobs, did not.
  `Start-Child` gives all three streams to every child it starts. Windows only:
  `server.py` has handed every child `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` from the start.

- **An antivirus block used to reach you as a wall of red.** `EngineShelf.bat`
  now recognises that particular refusal and says what happened, that it is a
  false positive, and the one command that allows it - instead of a parse error
  naming a line that has nothing to do with it.

- **Windows releases ship the PowerShell as it is written.** The build used to
  strip comments and blank lines from the six `.ps1` files it packages: 1,883 of
  5,183 lines, `gui\server.ps1` from 2,248 down to 1,392. Against anyone reading
  an interpreted script that buys nothing, and it left the file Defender actually
  reads denser than the one in the repository, with none of its own prose left to
  say what it was doing. `--ps-strip` puts it back for anyone who wants it. The
  macOS and Linux builds are unchanged - bash and Python are still wrapped.

## Upgrading

Replace the `EngineShelf` folder with the one from this release. Anyone whose
1.1.8 refused to open needs this one; anyone whose 1.1.8 opens is welcome to
stay on it.

If your antivirus still objects, allow the folder - in PowerShell as
Administrator, with the path to the `app` folder inside it:

    Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "C:\path\to\EngineShelf\app"

and please report it at https://www.microsoft.com/wdsi/filesubmission, which is
what gets the false positive cleared for everyone else.

Nothing else needs doing. Browsers you have downloaded, the profiles they run
with and any Docker images you have built are untouched.
